title: Token Fabric — Rate Lens prototype for role-aware cost slicing and export flows
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Background: Product teams need a compact, role-aware UI to understand per-token unit economics across routes, models, and teams. Current Console cost surfaces give aggregate spend but lack an interactive lens for token-level attribution, pivoting, and export presets for finance/engineering reviews.

Goals: 1) Ship a high-fidelity prototype of the 'Rate Lens' — an in-console panel that surfaces token-sliced cost breakdowns, contribution sparklines, and export-ready line items. 2) Support role-aware views (developer, team-lead, billing-admin) with sensible defaults and CSV/JSON export presets. 3) Demonstrate performance tradeoffs + propose a pragmatic aggregation strategy for production.

Scope: UX flows for: overview card, per-route token breakdown, top contributor table (prompt template, model, route, user/team), per-token sparkline for time series, attribution pivot controls (by model/route/team), and export modal with templates (Billing CSV, Engineering trace, Audit JSON). Includes desktop and tablet mocks.

Key interactions and microcopy: - 'Rate Lens' toggle on route detail page. - Attribution drawer: click contributor -> show sample prompts + percentage contribution. - Export modal: presets (Billing, Audit, Full), time range quick picks, role-aware field masking (PII or user email redaction).

Acceptance criteria: - Figma screens for all states (empty, partial data, full) linked in comments. - Usability test notes from 6 participants (design observations + 3 prioritized improvements). - Engineering-validated aggregation plan (daily pre-aggregates + per-request cache for 7d window). - Export CSV matches billing schema and includes SKU mapping.

Trade-offs/Notes: - Fine-grained per-invocation attribution is expensive; prototype should demonstrate sampling + pre-aggregation to keep latency/cost reasonable. - UI will show 'estimated' badge for sampled data. - Security: exports must respect RBAC and KMS masking policies.

Related artifacts: Figma prototype, PRD, prototype dashboard query, and a spike branch for pre-aggregation logic (links in comments).
comments: 2025-11-13 — Initial kickoff: scoped 5pt spike. PM (Eleanor Chen) requested a billing CSV sample and a compact route-level card for the runbook.

2025-11-18 — Design draft 1 uploaded to Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/token-fabric-rate-lens — includes overview card, attribution table, and export modal. Feedback from design review: simplify pivot controls and surface 'cost per successful token' metric.

2025-11-20 — Engineering sync (Rajiv Gupta): flagged compute cost for full per-invocation attribution. Suggested approach: daily pre-aggregates + 1-hour sliding cache for recent requests. Rajiv created spike branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-console/pull/9821.

2025-11-25 — Usability test session: 6 participants (3 devs, 2 finance, 1 ops). Key findings: export presets were helpful; finance wanted normalized SKU column; devs wanted quick link to sample prompts. Action: add 'sample prompt' drawer and SKU normalization in CSV.
2025-11-28 — PM review (Eleanor Chen): requested role-aware masking rules be explicit in the export modal and a confirmation when exporting >100k rows. Added to acceptance criteria.

2025-12-01 — Design handoff: Figma annotated with tokens and interaction notes; shared Confluence PRD: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COST/pages/TF-Rate+Lens. Waiting on engineering capacity for frontend spike.

2025-12-02 — Current status: In Review. Design lead (Mika Patel) requested accessibility review for table and modal; assigned to Accessibility sprints. Next: finalize copy and confirm pre-aggregate schema with backend (ENG-4112).
